To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
neuronal activity was significantly reduced on error trials in all of the investigated extrastriate cortical areas, independent of the hierarchical position in the dorsal visual system.

the neuronal response to a visual stimulus is reduced in extrastriate areas of the macaque dorsal pathway if the stimulus motion is unexpected, i.e. if the monkey makes an error in judging the stimulus motion direction, and that this activity reduction is not dependent on cortical hierarchical position, but rather on the stimulus contrast and the decision made.

the activity of direction selective cells in four areas of the dorsal visual pathway, V3A, MT, MST and STP, is reduced on error trials in a task that required a decision about the direction of a moving visual stimulus, and the reduction is similar in all of the areas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neuronal correlates of decision processes in the visual system.
the neuronal correlates of attention and expectation in the visual system.
the question of how information is encoded in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
decision processes do not depend on the hierarchical position of a visual area in the dorsal visual stream.
the decision‐related activity reduction in the dorsal visual system does not depend on cortical hierarchy.
the activity reduction in all visual areas is not related to decision‐making processes, but rather to a lack of attention.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dorsal visual pathway is not involved in decisions, but rather in sensory processing.
decision processes in the macaque brain depend more on the stimulus than the hierarchy in the visual pathway.
decision‐related activity in visual cortex is not a hierarchical phenomenon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neuronal activity reduction on error trails does not depend on the cortical hierarchy in the dorsal pathway.
the reduction in activity on error trials in the dorsal visual processing hierarchy is independent of the hierarchical position of a visual area.
decision-related activity in the dorsal visual stream is not hierarchically organized.
